text:
incident-bot: Pager alert: spike in 5xx and 429 across gateway-eu-1 starting at 08:12 UTC. Aggregated error rate 12% (baseline <0.5%). Related signals: increased queue depth on frontend, backend timeouts. Auto-escalation to oncall.
samira: looking now. do we know scope? any customers in SLO breach?
jon: getting metrics — 5xx concentrated on /v1/generate and /v1/chat, originating from a small set of upstream proxies. some 429s first, then 5xx. looks like quota enforcement is returning 429, but gateway is surfacing 5xx when backend rejects bursts.
maya: tagging logs: "rate_limiter: bucket_apply_error tenant=acme-corp action=reject". sending tail.
ash: can you paste the exact log lines? patching blind is risky.
maya: ```
2026-03-15T08:11:48Z ERROR rate_limiter bucket_apply failed tenant=acme-corp bucket=global-per-tenant cause=overlap-misapply
2026-03-15T08:11:49Z WARN gateway handler: upstream timeout tenant=acme-corp id=req-7f3a
2026-03-15T08:11:50Z ERROR http: 502 bad gateway tenant=acme-corp detail="upstream reset"
```
samira: interesting — "overlap-misapply" means the rollout script assigned a stricter quota policy to multiple proxies by mistake. who ran the quota rollout today?
jon: ops-bot shows a deployment at 07:55 UTC from @ash that included a quota policy patch: /infra/rate-limiter/policies/global_rollout.yaml
ash: yep that was me. I pushed a config to tighten burst windows for a subset of tenants for cost testing. I didn't expect the policy to overlap with the gateway enforcer buckets.
samira: ok immediate mitigation: revert the policy or whitelist high-throughput tenants. which is faster?
maya: revert is safe but will take ~5m to propagate. whitelist patch can be applied to the gateway layer in <2m but requires exact tenant list.
jon: customer impact — top 10 tenants by QPS show 50-80% elevated errors. SLA risk for two enterprise customers. product-ops: FYI.
product-ops: got it — starting customer comms for the two affected tenants. triage window estimate?
samira: do a quick rollback of the policy in config repo, trigger restart of rate-limiter pods in eu cluster, and temp-enable gateway fallback to older rate-limiter-mapping. I'll coordinate.
ash: rolling back now: ```bash
git revert --no-edit 7a3b9f2
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/rate-limiter-eu
``` 
ops-bot: Rollout invoked by ash: revert 7a3b9f2; rollout restart queued (job id rl-772)
jon: adding immediate gateway mitigation: set gateway to 429->queue-fallback rather than 5xx so clients get explicit throttles instead of internal errors. patching nginx-map
maya: patch applied to gateway-eu-1: added header X-Rate-Limit-Action: throttle for matched tenants. Reloading gateway config.
incident-bot: Config reload completed on gateway-eu-1 at 08:16:12 UTC.
samira: monitoring graphs — 429 count spiked marginally then dropped, 5xx tanked from 12% -> 1.8% within 90s. queue depth normalized.
jon: good. follow-up: need to fix policy rollout automation to prevent overlapping bucket id assignments. right now the new policy reused bucket id 'global-per-tenant' and overwrote existing mapping.
maya: agreed. I'll capture exact repro: rollout script merges on key 'bucket', missing uniqueness check.
ash: note: the cost-testing change was intended for a canary subset but PR had label prod=true by mistake. will open PR to change to canary flag.
product-ops: customers notified about incident start/mitigation. CS will send targeted follow-ups to the two affected customers with timeline and mitigation steps.
samira: handing off to next oncall for postmortem & follow-up. oncall rotation: @jon will take ownership for the post-incident review. add runbook items: revert gating, unique-bucket validations, canary gating on config push, and a postmortem timeline.
jon: taking handoff. I'll collate logs and open the incident postmortem doc. initial severity SEV2 given customer impact; will consider SEV1 if SLAs breached.
maya: saving logs and metrics snapshot: ```
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/recent?service=gateway-eu-1&from=2026-03-15T08:00&to=2026-03-15T08:20" > /tmp/gw-eu-spike.json
``` 
ops-bot: Incident closed in channel: mitigation applied; monitoring stable for 10m. Please continue postmortem in #incidents-postmortems.
samira: thanks all. action items: (1) rollback validated (ash), (2) patch rollout script (maya), (3) config PR canary gating (ash), (4) postmortem & customer notes (jon/product-ops). I'll follow up tomorrow for RCA.
jon: leaving note for next oncall: watch for any late cascading 5xx from downstream caches — we saw a delayed retry storm around 08:14. keep alarm thresholds lower for 30m.
maya: tagging logs/investigation artifacts to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2102345678
incident-bot: Pager summary: Mitigated (policy rollback + gateway throttle fallback). Root cause: quota policy misapply causing aggressive 429s and gateway-level 5xx cascade. Next steps: automation fixes and canary enforcement.
